case_open: A night-shift nurse in a 1994 coastal ER discovers a label printer that prints the name and time of death of a patient before they arrive. The first slip names a child who arrives 35 minutes early. Is the machine supernatural, or is it something else?

lead_internal_arc.starting_state: A practical, protocol-driven night-shift nurse, haunted by a patient's death she filed as 'unavoidable'. She trusts only what she can measure and avoids emotional involvement.
lead_internal_arc.ending_state: She accepts that the machine reflects her own choices, not fate. She stops fighting and takes responsibility for her decisions, finally resolving her guilt and gaining agency.
lead_internal_arc.arc_type: From denial to acceptance of responsibility

act_structure.name: Setup
act_structure.summary: Iris begins her shift. The machine prints a name + 03:47; she discards it. At 03:12 a father carries in a child with that name. End of ch1: 35 minutes left. In ch2, she tries to warn, but a second patient dies at their printed time. Doubt: is the machine warning her, or aiming her?

act_structure.name: Complications
act_structure.summary: Iris realizes every name is a patient she personally triaged. Marguerite mutters 'it only ever prints your handwriting.' In ch4-5, Iris tries to resist, rerouting a patient; her refusal causes the death. In ch6, she finds Marguerite's old logbook: same machine, same pattern 30 years ago—Marguerite tried to outrun it and stopped nursing.

act_structure.name: Crisis
act_structure.summary: Iris tests the machine by doing nothing—no names print, confirming it responds to her choices, not fate. Core reveal (ch8): the machine reflects her hand. Last year's death was also her choice. Then a slip prints: IRIS CALLAHAN and a time.

act_structure.name: Resolution
act_structure.summary: Iris stops resisting. She accepts a death she cannot prevent instead of causing one by fighting, and burns the machine. It goes silent. She survives, her guilt resolved. At dawn, an identical printer is delivered, factory-sealed, shipped from the hospital where Marguerite worked—it already has a slip printed.
